sourceEnglishObjective: Say what you and the crew do every day with regular verbs
candidateObjective: Describe a crew's habitual workday with times and present-form verbs.
candidateFocus: The ～ます form expresses repeated or scheduled actions. ～ています can describe an ongoing job or work habit. Mark a specific time with に; use 毎週 and 週に to talk about weekly routines.
curriculumAdaptationNote: Source objective teaches Spanish regular verbs for habitual crew work. Japanese ～ます, ～ています, time marker に and weekly expressions need a distinct qualified curriculum decision, including the work-habit versus current-action sense.

cards.reviewNote: Source el día names a day; archived 一日 can mean one full day or all day. Choose a context-specific standalone headword.
Source la semana names the week; archived 一週間 expresses a duration of one week. The Reader uses five days per week, so choose the time sense.

cards.candidateJapanese: 屋根の仕事をしています。
cards.archivedJapanese: 屋根の仕事をしています。
七時に屋根に上がります。
cards.reviewNote: Source says only we go up at seven; archived Japanese adds the roof. Decide whether this added destination is justified by the Reader context.

cards.candidateJapanese: どこに住んでいますか。
cards.archivedJapanese: どこに住んでいますか。

cards.sourceEnglish: We clean up at the end.
cards.archivedEnglish: We clean up at the end.

reader.sourceSpanish: Trabajo en techos cinco días a la semana.
reader.sourceEnglish: I work on roofs five days a week.
reader.candidateJapanese: 週に五日、屋根の仕事をしています。
reader.archivedJapanese: 週に五日、屋根の仕事をしています。
reader.archivedEnglish: I work on roofs five days a week.

reader.sourceSpanish: La cuadrilla llega a la obra a las seis de la mañana.
reader.sourceEnglish: The crew gets to the jobsite at six in the morning.
reader.candidateJapanese: 作業班は朝六時に現場に着きます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 作業班は朝六時に現場に着きます。
reader.archivedEnglish: The crew gets to the jobsite at six in the morning.

reader.archivedJapanese: 七時に屋根に上がります。
reader.reviewNote: Source says we go up at seven; archived Japanese adds the roof. Preserve the source's unspecified destination or obtain a source decision.

reader.sourceSpanish: Mi compañero corta las tejas y yo clavo.
reader.sourceEnglish: My coworker cuts the shingles and I nail.
reader.candidateJapanese: 同僚はシングル材を切り、私は釘を打ちます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 同僚はシングル材を切り、私は釘を打ちます。
reader.archivedEnglish: My coworker cuts the shingles and I drive nails.
reader.reviewNote: Source describes the coworker cutting shingles and speaker driving nails; preserve as a workday report, not an independently reviewed work procedure.

reader.sourceSpanish: Comemos el almuerzo a las doce.
reader.candidateJapanese: 正午に昼食を食べます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 正午に昼食を食べます。

reader.sourceSpanish: Por la tarde, la cuadrilla baja el material viejo.
reader.sourceEnglish: In the afternoon, the crew brings down the old material.
reader.candidateJapanese: 午後、作業班は古い資材を下ろします。
reader.archivedJapanese: 午後、作業班は古い資材を下ろします。
reader.archivedEnglish: In the afternoon, the crew brings down the old material.

reader.sourceEnglish: We clean up at the end of the day.
reader.candidateJapanese: 一日の最後に片づけます。
reader.archivedJapanese: 一日の最後に片づけます。
reader.archivedEnglish: We clean up at the end of the day.
